about.title: Software, architecture
about.paragraph1: I’ve been programming since 2013 and working professionally since 2020. I’ve built web applications, backends and mobile apps, and today I also connect software with electronics. React and TypeScript are where I have the longest track record, but I choose the technology to fit the problem, not the other way round.
about.paragraph2: In my professional work, I’ve worked on software architecture and as a Tech Lead while continuing to write code. I therefore tested architectural decisions directly in the implementation instead of treating them as a separate stage. I take the same approach to personal projects: I start with a concrete problem, choose the tools and bring the solution to a working state.
about.journeyIntro: I started with projects focused entirely on software.
about.redarkText: began with a custom WordPress theme, and migrating it to React and Gatsby taught me to plan a technology change without losing a working service or its SEO. With
about.dashboardText: I moved beyond software alone — months of independent learning, building electronics and working around Arduino’s constraints showed me how code behaves in a physical device.
about.systemsIntro: Later, I began building larger systems and integrating them with physical devices.
about.smartHomeText: brought together React, a Node.js backend and device communication. Daily use required tests, logging and monitoring that help me find problems quickly. In
about.vhsText: , I had to combine software with mechanical design, electronics and 3D printing, then fit all the components inside a real VCR enclosure.
about.aiPrefix: I worked professionally on AI-powered tools before coding assistants became widespread. With
about.aiMiddle: I used AI throughout the process, from writing the specification and breaking the work into stages to conducting my own code review. In
about.aiSuffix: , AI helped me configure Linux and understand the poorly documented communication with a Huawei modem, allowing me to devote more attention to the electronics, enclosure and reliability of the entire device.
